title: Federal transmission support can be real while the line is still unbuilt, withdrawn, or not yet delivering service
source_unit: U.S. Department of Energy Transmission Facilitation Program selection, financing, and project-status pages
geography: United States interregional transmission projects selected through DOE capacity-contract rounds

denominator.unit: capacity-contract projects listed across DOE first and second selection rounds

listed_capacity_contract_projects.unit: projects across two DOE selection rounds

second_round_commitment_context.unit: billion dollars; approximate DOE commitment context reported for second-round selections

projects_with_termination_or_withdrawal_.unit: listed projects: SWIP-N, Cross-Tie, Twin States, and Cimarron Link

remaining_projects_described_with_planne.unit: Southline, Aroostook, Southern Spirit, and Southline Phase 2

energized_transmission_service.value: not established for the listed project set
energized_transmission_service.unit: construction complete and line energized and ready for service

observations.method: Review of DOE program rules and current project-selection/status pages; project names and status notices are kept as listed by DOE and are not treated as a construction or operating dataset.
observations.uncertainty: The selections page does not provide a complete project-level denominator for construction or energization, and a termination or withdrawal can be followed by replacement financing or a redesigned project. Planned capacity and award amounts do not establish delivered electricity, rate effects, reliability, or household benefit.
observations.subgroup: DOE Transmission Facilitation Program capacity-contract selections in the first and second rounds; projects span multiple states and regional transmission contexts.
observations.counterinterpretation: Status changes may be normal portfolio management in a revolving program rather than evidence of program failure. DOE can repurpose conditional funds, and projects without a termination notice may still be progressing through permitting, financing, or construction.

related_sources.claim: DOE describes conditional selection, capacity contracts, cost recovery, and payment only after an energized line is ready to provide service.

boundary: This record measures DOE's federal support mechanism and listed project-status changes. It does not establish a national transmission completion rate, project failure rate, construction or energization for each remaining project, delivered electricity, rate incidence, reliability, local consent, environmental impact, or household benefit.
